_comment: The model registry. Read by openhands_f2p/models.py; F2P_MODELS_FILE points
elsewhere. Editing this file is how a model or a gateway is added -- no Python
Profiles are matched against the bare model id by glob, FIRST MATCH WINS, so
order matters: put exact names above their wildcards. The last entry should stay
Every field is optional except 'match'. Omitted fields take the defaults shown in
ModelProfile. 'native_tool_calling' has three states: true forces the native API,
false makes the SDK emulate calls through the prompt, and leaving it out says
nothing and lets the SDK decide -- which is not the same as false.
Keep 'note' honest and specific. It is the only place the reason for a value
survives, and a bare number here teaches the next person nothing.

providers.name: litellm-proxy
providers.note: The gateway this project has always run against. The model id carries no provider of its own, so litellm needs the prefix to know where to send it.

models.note: The agent model every measurement in this project was taken with, on exactly these values -- 32000 came from .env, not from the old hardcoded 16000, and recording the wrong one here would have halved the budget the moment that variable was unset. Follows a numbered sequence literally and calls the optional checks in roughly three runs out of five.

The judge, and usable as the agent model. Through this gateway it answers with a text preamble in choices[0] and the tool call in choices[1]; the SDK reads the first, so the agent recorded zero actions in twelve seconds until picks_first_choice=false routed it through MultiChoiceLLM. The flag is the cause, not a preference -- do not copy it to a model that answers with one choice.

Untested as the agent model. Same family as gpt-5-mini, so the response shape and tool calling are expected to work unchanged -- which is the reason to try it first when stepping down. Give it its own measured values once a run exists; until then it inherits the gpt-5-mini ones, which is a guess.

Untested. Served as openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-20b -- pass that full id, since the prefix is part of the gateway's name for it. Needs its own entry rather than falling to gpt-*: profile matching uses the bare id, so without this line it would silently take gpt-5-mini's tuning. Check native tool calling before a full set; an emulated tool call is a different experiment.

Served as openrouter/qwen/qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct -- pass that full id, the prefix is part of the gateway's name for it. Measured once, on the evaluation ten: 4/10, $0.28, and unusable as a ladder rung as served. OpenRouter routed every call to Novita, and 113 of 244 replies came back as a message object with no `content` key and no `tool_calls` key at all -- `{"role": "assistant", "provider_specific_fields": {...nulls}}`, finish_reason `stop`, with 45-1000 completion tokens billed for each one. Three empties in a row trip OpenHands' stuck detector and end the run, so three instances died having written nothing. That is a transport defect, not the model: every test it did finish reached 100% changed-line coverage. Before reading another number from it, route around Novita or set native_tool_calling false, and re-measure. Note also that no call was served from cache (cache_read_tokens 0), so each one paid full price for the whole prompt.

Untested. Served as qwen/qwen3-14b. Smoke-test one instance before committing a set: the failure modes worth ruling out first are emulated tool calling and a response that puts the call somewhere other than choices[0], which is what cost gpt-5.5 a wasted run.

Untested, and the smallest of the ladder. Served as meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct. The point of running it is to find where the tools start to matter, so a poor score here is a result rather than a fault.

The judge, from 2026-09-24. One call per instance and only on a fail-to-pass YES, so an arm of seventy pays for roughly forty. Chosen over gpt-5.5 deliberately and it is the expensive part of a run now, so the judge's own cost is worth reading separately from the agent's. Probed before being made the default: one choice, content in choices[0], finish_reason stop -- none of the gpt-5.5 quirk that needed picks_first_choice, and the judge makes no tool calls in any case. Runs made before this date were judged by gpt-5.5 and are read against later ones without adjustment; the concept verdict does not feed the F2P result, so the difference changes no score.
Anything else on the gateway, on the settings measured for gpt-5-mini.
Untested here. Present so the shape of adding a provider is visible rather than hypothetical.
Fallback, so resolution never fails. The defaults are the gpt-5-mini ones, which is a guess for any model that lands here -- give it its own entry above once you have run it.
